newsitem.title: USA: U.S. resource use level not sustainable - S.F. Fed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. resource use level not sustainable - S.F. Fed.

text.p: The current level of resource utilization in the U.S. economy is not sustainable in the long run without triggering inflationary pressures, the head of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco said.
"The current level of resource utilization is not sustainable without inflation becoming a problem," San Francisco Fed president Robert Parry told an audience of bankers and businessmen here.

In a brief speech, Parry said the key question going forward was whether the economy would slow to more sustainable levels, adding that recent economic data suggest growth was cooling off from sizzling first quarter levels.
"I think the important question is whether the economy is going to slow to a more sustanaible pace, and my answer is that there may be some grounds for optimism," Parry said.

"Very recent data give hints of slowing from the torrid pace of the first quarter. I think this is seen most clearly in the employment numbers where the rate of growth of employment in the past two months has slowed," Parry added.
Parry also said a strong dollar may help to slow U.S. exports as well as control inflation in the near future.
"The higher value of the dollar will likely slow the growth of exports as well as being a force constraining inflation directly," Parry said.
The head of the San Francisco Fed stressed the need for slower growth to avoid future inflation problems.

"In summary, the transition to slower, more sustainable growth rates for the economy is necessary to avoid future inflation problems and it's necessary, in my view, to ensure future prosperity," Parry said.
